claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a bulk density of approximately 10.21 g cm−3.
Fully dense, as-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high room-temperature strength.
Fully dense, as-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at approximately 1000 °C.
HfMoTaTiZr can be fabricated as a lattice-structured component by LPBF.
Laser powers of 200–400 W, scan speeds of 300–600 mm s−1, and layer thicknesses of 30–50 µm are suitable LPBF parameter ranges for this intervention.
Lattice unit-cell sizes of approximately 0.5–2.0 mm are suitable for the proposed HfMoTaTiZr component.
The LPBF lattice should be built and consolidated under an inert-gas environment.
The engineered lattice removes non-load-bearing solid volume.
The engineered lattice preserves local load-bearing features.
Reducing the solid volume proportionally decreases the component's effective density.
Introducing lattice geometry does not alter the base HfMoTaTiZr chemistry.
Preservation of the base-alloy chemistry and refractory matrix retains high-temperature strength.
The lattice structure will reduce effective density by more than 20% relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The lattice structure will retain at least 90% of the as-cast room-temperature mechanical strength.
The lattice structure will retain at least 90% of the as-cast mechanical strength at approximately 1000 °C.
The proposed lattice is applicable in oxidizing environments up to approximately 1000 °C.
The proposed lattice is applicable under loads approaching its yield strength.
Above approximately 1200 °C, oxidation may necessitate protective treatments.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires a density decrease greater than 20%, but the rejection rule only falsifies density decreases below 10%. A measured decrease between 10% and 20% would violate the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.

The hypothesis requires strength retention at both room temperature and elevated temperature, whereas the rejection rule explicitly addresses only high-temperature strength falling below 90%; inadequate room-temperature strength is not specified as a rejection condition.
